sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it, without tripping any of the guards below:

rules.text: At least one {{entity_noun}} can be identified from the phrase and its relationship summary.

The phrase and its relationship summary say something substantive about the identified {{entity_noun}} — describing an activity, arrangement, or dealing that involves it — rather than only naming it, listing it, or mentioning it in passing. Which party is involved is not this condition's subject; [SCR-3] decides that.

It is the manufacturer itself that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the identified {{entity_noun}} — not a customer, supplier, distributor, or other third party that the manufacturer merely relates to.

children.text: Summaries refer to the manufacturer in question only as "the manufacturer", never by name; other companies may appear by name or by their standing. A brand, trade name, former name, division, plant, or business unit of the manufacturer IS the manufacturer itself. A statement about the manufacturer's parent company or a sister brand counts as one about the manufacturer itself, and does not fail this condition merely for being attributed to them — unless the summary shows the activity belongs to that company alone and not to the manufacturer.

That a third party is named does not on its own fail this condition. What decides it is which party {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the identified {{entity_noun}}: where the manufacturer supplies or sells to a party that operates in it, it is the manufacturer that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} that {{entity_noun}}.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate does not reject the phrase — another candidate may still qualify:

rules.text: The manufacturer's involvement in the identified {{entity_noun}} is only aspirational, hoped-for, planned, or discontinued, rather than current and actual.
